question: The word Kathak is derived from the Sanskrit word Katha, which means:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Story**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'kathak'** is derived from the Sanskrit word **'katha'**, which means **story**__.
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form that originated in Northern India and is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• Historically, **Kathak** dancers, known as **kathakars** or storytellers, would narrate stories from epics and mythology through dance.
 
• The dance form has evolved over centuries and now incorporates elements of both Hindu and Persian cultures.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **word 'kathak'** comes from the tradition of **storytellers** or **kathakars** who would recount tales from the great epics and ancient scriptures.
 
• **Kathak** has three main gharanas (schools) - **Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras**, each with its own unique style and emphasis.
 
• It is performed to the accompaniment of classical music, with instruments such as the **tabla** and **harmonium** being central to the performance.
 
• The dance form also includes the use of **ghungroos** (bells) tied around the ankles, which add rhythmic complexity to the performance.
